item.title: Version 26.10
item.description:
DynaMoE

v26.10
High-Performance MoE Inference Engine for Apple Silicon

What's New in 26.10

No limit on agent steps:

The Max Multi-Step Agent Iterations slider stopped at 100, so a long autonomous task could not say "keep going until it is done" and always ended on a count. A No limit switch beside the slider now uncaps the run: the slider keeps the user's last finite number and goes inert, so turning the switch back off restores it rather than leaving a sentinel behind. Both agent loops read the budget through one rule, so the weights path and a cloud run cannot disagree about what "no limit" means, and the cap is resolved per step so a settings change applies to a run already in flight. An uncapped run ends on the model's own complete, a tool loop guard (a failed-call streak, a repeated call, the search budget), the model's context limit (the KV budget for local weights, the context window for a cloud provider), or Stop, and the run-end status names only the limit that actually applied, distinguishing a run the model completed, one a tool loop guard stopped, and one that spent its budget. Settings search finds it under "no limit" and "unlimited".

Cloud turns ask for the provider's cache:

A cloud agent run re-sends its whole history on every step, and the app neither asked for the provider's prefix cache nor showed what it was billed. Every request now carries a stable session identity (x-session-id / x-session-affinity, a hash of the conversation rather than its UUID) so a router keeps one conversation on one replica, and providers registered with Session affinity + cache key also send OpenAI's prompt_cache_key. Both hints are recoverable: a provider that rejects the body field is retried once without it, and the refusal is remembered for the rest of the process only when the retry succeeds and the refusal names the field, so a vague or transient 400 (a concurrency limit, a rate-limit message) cannot switch caching off. The cache key's refusal is remembered per endpoint and model, the affinity headers' per endpoint, so one model on a shared gateway cannot silence its neighbours; a built-in's read-only row offers Forget Refusals. The system prompt is no longer rewritten mid-run, so each step extends the cached prefix instead of invalidating it. Cache reads are decoded from every wire shape they arrive in (prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens, prompt_cache_hit_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens) and merged across a stream's chunks rather than replaced: the Request Log row reads 1,000→50 tok · 800 cached, its detail sheet splits 800 cached, 100 cache write, 600 billable, and the Console line carries cached=800. Re-send Images (Settings → Cloud Providers → Request Behaviour, default on) decides whether every picture rides every request or only the newest user turn's; pictures from earlier turns become a one-line notice instead of a repeated charge.

A cloud conversation that knows its ceiling and its bill:

Two registration facts feed the displays, both set from defaults because no provider catalog publishes them: context windows per model (dynamoe_cloud_<provider>_context, model=window entries) and prices per model (dynamoe_cloud_<provider>_pricing, JSON in USD per million tokens with cached_input and cache_write_input rates). With a window recorded the header shows tokens · N% of window, where the figure is the context the last request carried (one meaning on every backend, so moving a conversation between a local and a cloud model no longer inflates it) and a send projected past 80% of the window compacts older history with the active provider model before spending the request. The reply budget is capped to the room that threshold leaves, so a Max Output Tokens setting larger than a small window's room is lowered rather than compacting forever against a wall it can never clear; a provider context_length_exceeded rejection compacts and retries that step once; a run may compact more than once as it refills its window, and one pass reads at most eight summarizer excerpts, with a longer history summarized as a head-and-tail excerpt that names how much middle history it omitted. /compact now uses the active provider model for a cloud conversation and honours /compact <focus>, so it works on a Mac without Apple Intelligence. With a price recorded, each turn's status line ends with its cost (1,204 billed in (1,000 of it cached) / 56 out · $0.0031) and the header carries the conversation's cumulative spend, summarizer requests included. A step that completed and reported no usage is counted from the app's own estimate and marked (est.), and no cost is invented for it from estimated tokens; a request that was sent and then stopped, failed or was cut off is charged from the same estimate, because the provider billed the prompt it received. A request the provider refused without running the model (an expired key, an unknown model, a rate limit, any 4xx) is not charged, and neither is anything that never left the Mac; a figure below a ten-thousandth of a dollar prints <$0.0001. Cloud compaction also shows its progress in the transcript, and its digest rides every step of the run.

Fixes

  • Stop during /compact: Stop used to commit the partial summary the cancelled summarizer returned and delete every message it never covered. The pass is now checked at each pass boundary and immediately before the rewrite, Stop reports itself instead of a failure or a success, and Stop in a compacting chat no longer cancels an unrelated chat's generation
  • A turn /compact cut short: A message larger than one summarizer request was truncated to fit and then deleted along with the summary, so the omitted tail was gone for good. Oversized turns are split across passes instead, which keeps every character while each request stays inside the budget
  • Two chats compacting at once: A single compaction flag let a pass in one chat clear the gate another pass still needed, so a send could land in a rewrite and Stop could cancel nothing. Manual compaction state is now keyed by conversation, with a run id so only the owning pass clears it
  • A finished cloud reply that read as cut off: A [DONE] arriving as the final line of a stream was discarded, so a complete answer was reported as a connection that closed early. The end of a stream is no longer dropped, and finish reasons are classified rather than matched by exact spelling, so only a recognised clean stop lets a summary replace the messages it was written from
  • Under the hood: The README and settings guide document the No limit switch, provider prompt caching, Re-send Images, context-window and price registration, and cloud compaction

item.title: Version 26.9
item.description:
DynaMoE

v26.9
High-Performance MoE Inference Engine for Apple Silicon

What's New in 26.9

Plan Mode:

A new read-only architect mode makes the agent investigate and propose before it touches anything. Enter it from the pill beside Turbo, with ⇧⌘P, or by typing /plan; it is a per-conversation mode, so one chat can be planning while another is coding. The write, edit, shell, git_commit, complete and every MCP tool are withheld rather than discouraged: absent from the prompt and from a cloud model's tools array, withheld from the constrained-sampling grammar, and refused by the tool executor if one is somehow emitted. Subagents inherit the restriction, including the Test Runner pipeline, so delegation cannot route around it. What remains is the reading half of the harness: file reads, glob/grep, codebase and symbol search, git_status / git_diff, web search and fetch, lint diagnostics, and tool discovery, plus a small read core loaded on entry so an investigation does not open with a discovery step. The model ends its answer with a pair of plan markers, which renders as an Implementation Plan card with Start coding, Code with Turbo and Revise plan; approving switches the conversation to Code Mode, re-arms the write tools and sends "Implement the plan." as an ordinary user turn. A cloud model that calls tools plans normally; a backend with no tool loop (the Apple on-device model, or a provider registered without tool support) refuses entry with a message rather than flipping a mode its turns could not honour. The mode is fixed for the length of a turn: the pill, /plan and the handoff are all refused while a turn is running, because the live turn's prompt, grammar and tool surface were built for the mode it started in, and an approval whose send is refused puts the conversation back in Plan Mode with the transcript unchanged.

Cloud providers from Settings:

Adding a remote provider used to mean editing Swift and rebuilding, so the only endpoint the app could reach was the one it shipped with. Settings → Cloud Providers → Add Provider… now registers any OpenAI-compatible endpoint at runtime: a display name, an immutable identifier that becomes its Keychain account and the cloud:// address saved with each conversation, the API base URL, an optional key written only to the Keychain, and an optional documentation link. The base must be https (plain http is accepted only on loopback), and a URL carrying user:password@ or a query string is refused rather than saved, because the key belongs in the API Key field and rides the Authorization header. Any endpoint that answers POST <base>/chat/completions with a Bearer key and lists its catalog over GET <base>/models works, and the model list tolerates the envelope differences between gateways. Test & Sync Models validates the key and registers the provider's chat models without spending a completion token, and the catalog fetch filters out embeddings, rerankers, speech, moderation and image generators so they cannot become pickable entries that fail on the first send. Remove deletes a custom provider's key, registered models, no-tools list and vision marks; a conversation pinned to one of its models then refuses to send with a reselect message instead of silently falling back to local weights. Editing a provider's base URL drops those registrations too, because they describe the server at the old address. Built-in Synthetic stays, cannot be edited or removed, and the registry can never be empty.

A summary you can still read:

/compact used to fold the conversation into two digests and then show only a marker, so the summary it had just produced survived only inside the prompt. The committed history now opens with an expandable card carrying the same general summary and detailed recap, followed by the marker naming how many messages were compacted. The card is display-only (the digests still travel in the system block), so nothing is sent twice and it costs no context, and it survives a relaunch, unlike the transient progress bubble it replaces. A copy button puts the whole digest on the clipboard.

Fixes

  • Messages that never appeared: A refused send or a failed model load wrote its reason to state nothing rendered, so the app looked like a dead button at exactly the moment it had something to say, while the feedback that did render (attachment refusals, queued prompts, the history banner) was inserted into the layout around the transcript and shrank it, moving the very text the user was reading. Everything the chat column says now floats in one layer above the composer that cannot resize any pane, with the transcript reserving the layer's height so nothing is held out of reach. Severity is read from the glyph each message already carried, so the tint cannot disagree with the copy; long-running work keeps a progress pill until it finishes instead of vanishing after six seconds; a prompt's ingest counters stay on the transcript row that already showed them instead of re-fading the pill and re-reading it aloud; the history banner sits under the header it used to cover for a whole session; and a failed engine load now records its long reason in the transcript, because a chat that cannot send is permanent rather than six seconds long. The Advanced Diagnostics settings tab went with it: its three buttons all depended on a buffer no reachable routine ever filled, so every press could only report failure
  • Images offered to models that cannot see them: The attach menu stayed enabled for a text-only model, so picking an image produced a generic refusal that never named the selected model, and sending an already-staged image offered the same "switch models to attach one" advice instead of the fix that applied. Both menu items are now disabled with a tooltip that explains why, the refusal names the selected model and the fix for the situation (switch models before attaching, or remove the attachment before sending), and switching models retracts a stale refusal or raises a fresh one for images already staged
  • Under the hood: The README and settings guide document Plan Mode, runtime provider setup and the compaction summary card

item.title: Version 26.8
item.description:
DynaMoE

v26.8
High-Performance MoE Inference Engine for Apple Silicon

What's New in 26.8

macOS 26 or later:

26.8 is built against the macOS 26 SDK, so it no longer launches on earlier versions and the update gate says so. The on-device Apple system model and /compact conversation compaction stay gated on Apple Intelligence as well.

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash:

A new model family runs locally, and it is a different class of model from anything else DynaMoE has served. Its forty layers split in two: the encoder half compresses the context into sparse rows and the decoder half reads them back, with latent attention over a compressed cache, six activated experts out of 384 per layer in MXFP4, and DeepSeek's Engram n-gram memory tables, roughly a hundred gigabytes of it, streamed a row at a time. Everything streams from NVMe instead of being held in RAM: the dense backbone is pinned once at load and the expert cache is wired so a read runs at the disk's own rate. It drives the whole turn path like any other family: its own prompt format with a graded Reasoning Effort line (Thinking High / Low / Off), tool calls in the dialect it was actually trained to emit so agent turns execute tools instead of answering prose, images through its built-in vision tower with the cost of a picture priced in the composer before you send it, and prefix reuse across turns so a follow-up re-prefills only what is new (24 of 31 positions reused, 10.7 s then 1.8 s on the published checkpoint). It is served over the local API too. Expect to need roughly half a terabyte of disk and a large-Unified-Memory Mac: the port prices its expert cache from available RAM and wires it for the length of a turn.

Nanbeige 4.3 and Q4/Q8 quantization for dense models:

A 33B dense checkpoint is now identified from its own shape rather than its name (it declares itself a plain Llama), so it keeps its real chat template, its <tool_response> tool turns and its qwen3_coder tool calls. A dense model has no experts to stream, so decode reads the entire weight set once per token: the new Quantize to Q4 / Q8 action (Models → ⋯) rewrites the weights into one contiguous quantized blob beside the snapshot, taking 66 GB to ~34 GB at Q8 and ~22 GB at Q4, with decode around 2.4x faster at Q4 and the published turn still answered token for token. The embedding and output head stay at full precision.

Longer context on every model:

The provisioned row ceiling now comes from the checkpoint's own max_position_embeddings instead of a flat 32,768, so a long-context model can actually use its context (Nanbeige 4.3 reaches 524,288 natively; the ceiling is capped at 262,144 rows). The RAM budget is still the authority that decides what fits, and raising the KV cache to FP8 is what lets a big model reach those lengths on a smaller Mac.

The local API server grew up:

The server that exposes the loaded model over OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs now speaks both protocols' front doors properly. It serves the models list and retrieve routes in each protocol's own shape, answers Anthropic's POST /v1/messages/count_tokens pre-flight from the turn's own planner (so the count it reports is the usage.input_tokens that turn reports), and serves the legacy POST /v1/completions text route. Image content parts work on both protocols, in every spelling either one allows, with remote URLs refused rather than fetched, and the models list finally says what the model can do: capabilities (vision, thinking, thinking levels, accepted reasoning_effort values), the checkpoint's own context_length, the max_prompt_tokens threshold the server actually refuses on, and a vision_cost range derived from the checkpoint's resize plan so a client can size a timeout before it sends a picture.

Images on cloud models:

Cloud turns can carry screenshots and photos. Deleting a conversation removes its image files, staged and queued images are never silently orphaned, and a provider rejection only downgrades a model when the error names the image part.

Fixes

  • Local server queueing: A request arriving while the app was generating was refused outright with a 503, and under a burst the queue was not serializing at all: twenty-four concurrent requests produced twenty-four turns at once instead of one after another. Requests now wait for whichever turn holds the engine, bounded by the existing queue timeout rather than a new setting, a client that waits past it is told whether it was waiting on other requests or on the app, and concurrent requests run strictly one at a time
  • Request fields that were answered as if they had not been sent: OpenAI's store: false is the one field whose entire meaning is "do not keep this", and it was never decoded, so with content capture on the request's prompt, answer and tool arguments were written to the log anyway; a client's refusal now withholds them and the log row says the client asked for it. The same unknown-key tolerance silently dropped max_completion_tokens (every request using OpenAI's newer spelling ran to the app default of up to 8,192 tokens), frequency_penalty and logit_bias (both now honoured on both OpenAI routes), and Anthropic's metadata. reasoning_effort was validated against this engine's own two words rather than the protocol's four, so minimal and medium (and medium is what OpenAI's SDK sends by default) were answered with a 400 that read as the client's mistake. A request asking for spoken output (modalities, audio) was answered with prose and no message.audio, leaving the client's parser waiting for a field nothing would send; the deprecated functions / function_call spelling was answered with prose and no error at all; web_search_options was dropped, returning ungrounded prose where citations were expected; Anthropic's output_config (JSON output) and mcp_servers were dropped; and one echoed redacted_thinking block refused an entire conversation over bytes this engine could not have read anyway. All of them are now either honoured or refused by name before any generation
  • Model identity: Every route advertised the loaded checkpoint's snapshot directory name as the model id, which for a hub snapshot is a commit hash: unusable as a path segment, unrecognisable in a log row, and different every time the same model was re-resolved. The id is now the repository's short name (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017), and the old snapshot name is still answered as an alias so a config written against an earlier version keeps resolving. Anthropic clients also get a models list and retrieve route they can actually decode, with a human model name in the field the protocol defines for it
  • Images over the API: The server refused every image content part with a message saying the local model understood text only, which stopped being true once the loaded checkpoint gained a vision tower; the same model read pictures in the chat window and rejected them over the API. Both wire spellings now decode into one form, the picture is placed in the turn that carried each one rather than moved in front of all the text, the expanded prompt is priced before the cache is provisioned, and the session identity includes the picture so a follow-up about a second image cannot reuse the first one's pinned prefix
  • Keychain prompts on every update: Installing a new version produced a "DynaMoE wants to use your confidential information" dialog for each stored credential, and the startup path could ask too. Credentials now live in the data protection keychain, where access is granted by the app's own code-signing identity instead of a per-item prompt, and nothing reads a secret at launch: whether one is stored is answered from item attributes, which macOS returns without a dialog. Credentials written by an earlier version are copied across once from the Stored Credentials card in Settings (Cloud Providers or Agent & Tools), one explained prompt per credential, with the old copy removed only after the new one reads back. A refused read now reports itself as refused instead of claiming no key is stored, and an MCP server blocked by an un-imported credential names the import it needs rather than reporting an unresolved token
  • Repacked models: A repack recorded an empty shape for every tensor, so a repacked Qwen 3.8 priced a routed expert's MLP at its 512-wide default while the weights are 640 wide and answered every prompt with gibberish; the packer now carries real shapes into both manifests, and the sparse-attention indexer's pick no longer depends on tensor order (which differed between a packed manifest and its safetensors source). An interrupted repack also left a zero-length expert layer beside finished ones that the loader preferred anyway, so expert reads ran past the end of the file; a packed model is now only preferred when every layer file is present and full, and repacking is atomic so an interruption cannot leave a half-written blob behind
  • Tool turns on the ChatML families: A turn that followed a tool result built its prompt two different ways (the live continuation opened its reasoning channel spelled one way while the rebuilt history opened another, and the assistant turn marker was emitted twice), so every tool call ended the conversation's reusable prefix and forced a full re-prefill. Both paths now produce the same bytes, a tool result is tagged as one, each family uses its own markup, and the same shape is used over the local API
  • Under the hood: Prefill now chunks for every family rather than only Gemma, so a long prompt's transient memory scales with the chunk instead of the whole prompt; the README and settings guide document DeepSeek V4.1, Nanbeige 4.3, the Q4/Q8 quantizer, and every request field this server accepts, honours or refuses

item.title: Version 26.7
item.description:
DynaMoE

v26.7
High-Performance MoE Inference Engine for Apple Silicon

What's New in 26.7

External tool servers (MCP):

The agent can now use tools that ship as separate programs or remote services instead of Swift compiled into the app. Servers are declared in one editable mcp.json (stdio child processes or Streamable HTTP endpoints) and speak the Model Context Protocol, surfacing as ordinary agent tools under mcp__<server>__<tool>. A new Settings card shows live status and handles add, edit, enable, restart, and remove, with both a form and a raw JSON editor. The file stays the source of truth (external edits are picked up without a restart, and deferred while a turn is running), credentials live in the Keychain behind ${keychain:...} tokens so they never touch disk, discovered tools cost zero prefill tokens until the model loads them, and every MCP call asks for approval unless Turbo Mode is on.

Corrected KV capacity rules:

A tools-enabled turn is no longer refused before prefill just because the machine cannot afford the 8,192-row agent reserve. The pre-launch check now prices the model's real sliding-window ring layout and the effective KV precision the allocator uses, treats the agent reserve as a preference the RAM budget caps rather than a veto, and refuses a turn only when the prompt itself cannot fit, so a few-thousand-token prompt runs again on a memory-constrained Mac. Rejections say what actually binds (budget, model footprint, precision, affordable rows) and reach API clients as a context_length_exceeded error; the new dynamoe_agent_session_floor key lowers the reserve when you need to.

Connected cloud providers (Synthetic):

Cloud inference becomes a third backend beside local weights and the Apple on-device model. Synthetic's models appear under Cloud Models in the composer, and a turn runs against the provider's OpenAI-compatible API with no engine, tokenizer, Metal buffers, or KV cache in the path. With Agent Tools on it uses the provider's native function calling, so streamed tool calls execute through the same harness as a local turn (approvals, Turbo Mode, loop guards, and the subagent report relay). Test & Sync Models validates the key and registers the provider's live chat models in one press, keys stay in the login Keychain, and switching to a cloud model releases any resident weights engine.

Selectable thinking levels:

Spark X2.6 adds a graded reasoning template, so the Thinking menu offers High, Low, and Off instead of a plain on/off switch for level-capable checkpoints. The choice is stored per conversation and rendered as reasoning_effort in both the in-app and API prompts; the OpenAI endpoint takes "reasoning_effort": "low" | "high", the Anthropic endpoint maps thinking.budget_tokens, and unsupported values are rejected with 400 instead of being silently ignored.

Transcript performance:

Long conversations render without stalling. Display cleanup, markdown parsing, and syntax highlighting are memoized per frame, follow-scroll is throttled to line-sized buckets, and very long paragraphs, quotes, reasoning, and code are drawn as bounded chunks so an oversized text view can no longer leave the transcript blank. The output-token and agent-step ceilings now match what the KV cache can actually provision.

Fixes

  • MCP reliability: A dead HTTP endpoint no longer keeps a Ready row with tools registered against a corpse, a server that cannot start stays Failed with its error until you retry it or change its config instead of relaunching in a loop, in-place rewrites of mcp.json are noticed rather than only atomic saves, a tool-list refresh keeps already-loaded tools loaded, and an external config edit waits for a pending approval or running tool call before it reconnects
  • MCP wire protocol: Oversized frames are refused even when they arrive newline-terminated, line scanning stays linear when bytes dribble in one at a time (a large frame could previously stall until timeout), the assembled event is bounded rather than each line alone, JSON-RPC request ids are echoed verbatim (string and zero-padded ids included), an abandoned request notifies the server so state-changing calls stop running remotely, and the protocol revision a server negotiated is used for every later request. Out-of-range timeouts are rejected at validation instead of trapping on connect, arguments round-trip as a JSON array, and credentials are written only after the form validates and rolled back if it does not
  • Cloud turns: A cloud turn never registered its own conversation with the agent harness, so a subagent it spawned could surface in the wrong transcript or never surface at all; cloud turns now claim their session and wait for in-flight subagents before relaying. Parallel tool calls that arrive without a stream index are no longer merged into one, a reply cut off by the output-token limit says so in the transcript, abandoned provider responses release their connection instead of lingering, and model rescans no longer probe the Keychain on the main thread
  • Live speed: A cloud turn read zero tokens per second while it was thinking and stayed diluted afterwards because only visible content was counted; reasoning and content are now counted together, and a provider-reported total still wins so the header speed matches the final footer number
  • Markdown and presets: Oversized paragraphs and quotes keep their bold, code, and link formatting instead of showing literal markers, and duplicate output-token presets are deduplicated so a constant colliding with a literal can no longer crash the settings pane
  • Settings window: On macOS 26 the unified toolbar's glass strip covered the top of the detail pane and clipped section headers as they scrolled; the pane now runs full height under a transparent titlebar, so content passes beneath the floating controls instead of disappearing
  • Under the hood: Spark X2.6 joins X2.5 in supported models, and the README and settings guide document MCP servers, cloud providers, and the corrected KV capacity rules

item.title: Version 26.6
item.description:
DynaMoE

v26.6
High-Performance MoE Inference Engine for Apple Silicon

What's New in 26.6

Local inference server:

The loaded model is now served on 127.0.0.1 through both OpenAI-compatible (/v1/chat/completions) and Anthropic-compatible (/v1/messages) APIs, so local coding agents and other tools can use DynaMoE with no external service involved. A new Server settings tab manages live status, port, API key, and a copyable endpoint; turns queue behind the engine with SSE streaming, heartbeats while queued, and protocol-correct errors; and stopping or restarting the server never interrupts an in-app response.

Multi-turn prefix reuse:

Follow-up API requests extend the previous turn's pinned KV prefix instead of re-prefilling the whole conversation. The server remembers each completed turn, reasoning included, and splices it back in only when the client's history matches the conversation that produced it; the prompt's date is pinned per session so the cached prefix stays valid; and reasoning round-trips for clients: Anthropic thinking blocks are signed so SDKs keep them, and the new "Reasoning in Content" setting folds reasoning into content for OpenAI-compatible clients that ignore the reasoning field. Agent loops that re-prefilled the entire prompt at every step now prefill seconds' worth of tokens.

Client-defined tools:

API requests that carry their own tool schemas now work: each turn teaches the engine the client's tool vocabulary and restores the previous registry afterwards, tool calls keep their ids and JSON nulls through the round trip, and forced tool choices the engine cannot enforce are rejected with a clear 400 instead of silently degrading.

Request log:

Every API request and every in-app chat, agent, and Apple Foundation Model turn now leaves a trace: metadata-only lines in Console.app plus a persisted request log browsable from the Server tab, with search, error filtering, a detail inspector, JSONL export, and a queue-wait vs. generation-time split. Bodies are opt-in behind the "Store Request Content" toggle, rows read as withheld when it is off, credentials are never logged, and the log prunes itself to 30 days / 20,000 rows.

Persistent memory settings:

The in-app memory mode and budget now persist across relaunches, and server turns honor them, so picking Unrestricted with an FP8 KV cache actually raises the server's KV capacity instead of being silently ignored.

Fixes

  • Memory accounting: Duplicated backbone buffers are no longer allocated once per model load (three resident copies were together holding 15.25 GB on a 16 GB Mac), the user-facing memory figure reports what the process actually holds (footprint plus cached weight pages) instead of resident pages that collapsed under swap pressure, and KV provisioning is clamped to the machine's RAM budget
  • OpenAI tool calls: Responses and stream deltas now encode tool calls under the wire format's tool_calls key; the previous camelCase key made them invisible to every OpenAI client, and client-defined tools were taught a call shape the engine's parser only recognized for built-in tool names
  • SSE streaming: Anthropic stream frames keep their data: prefix (standard parsers silently discarded the payloads), streaming deltas withhold suffixes that could still grow into a configured stop sequence, and a repaired snapshot is never re-sent where a client cannot replace it
  • Oversized prompts: A prompt that cannot fit the machine's KV cache allocation is rejected (or its max_tokens ratcheted) in milliseconds instead of overrunning the cache and grinding for the better part of an hour; SSE heartbeats now run for the full turn instead of going silent during prefill, and Metal allocation failures now print where they happened
  • Queue and lifecycle correctness: A queue-wait timeout fires at its deadline even when an earlier turn is stalled, cancelling a request cancels its queued work instead of launching against an abandoned connection, the server toggle and Restart reconcile to the persisted setting once a shutdown drains, and Restart applies a freshly typed port
  • Under the hood: Rust dependencies upgraded (uniffi 0.28 to 0.32, safetensors 0.4 to 0.8, tokenizers 0.20 to 0.23) and Sparkle 2.9.6 to 2.10.0, the regenerated Swift bindings gain Sendable conformances, and a bindgen change that could hang every Xcode 27 build is fixed

item.title: Version 26.5
item.description:
DynaMoE

v26.5
High-Performance MoE Inference Engine for Apple Silicon

What's New in 26.5

Apple Foundation Model support:

Chat with Apple's on-device Foundation Model, with live activity indicator, smoothed streaming, and a per-turn history budget so the transcript honors its context window.

/compact Conversation Compaction:

Manual /compact slash command (opencode-style) that folds the conversation into two AFM digests — a rolling general summary plus a detailed recap of recent work — injected into every later prompt on both backends. Transactional (a failed model leaves chat untouched), chunked for long histories, includes tool-call records. Auto-compact on context limits is deliberately deferred to a follow-up.

Settings Glow-up:

Reworked settings into a sidebar-driven layout matching macOS System Settings: sliders + editable numeric fields replacing steppers, shaded group backgrounds, three-per-row sampling controls with precise inputs, and an updated settings guide.

Composer polish:

Chat composer default height reduced by a third; minimum fits one line with trimmed chrome.

Gemma 4 26B A4B support:

DynaMoE now loads and runs `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` end to end: architecture detection, the interleaved sliding/global attention layers (per-head q/k norms, proportional RoPE on global layers), the dense+MoE decoder block, and the `<|channel>thought … ` reasoning template. Verified element-for-element against the HF reference forward pass.

Fixes

  • Chat Formatting: Stop chat messages from truncating and overlapping when selected
  • RAM telemetry: "Process Heap" mislabeled RSIZE as the Activity Monitor/Xcode number (actually`phys_footprint`, overstated up to 5.2×), and Working Set RAM double-counted weight bytes (~12.9 GB shown was really ~5 GB), evicting experts early. Now shows genuine footprint + a new "Unified Memory Cache" line; budget decisions use RSIZE alone. Also removed the pread-into-read-only-mmap prefetch path that was a silent no-op (EFAULT).
  • FP8 slow at long context: FP8 KV-cache decode never got the FP16 path's flash-decoding split-K kernels — one thread per head over the whole context. Added FP8 chunked scan kernels for Spark and Ornith, and disabled JetSpec under FP8 (its verify kernels would corrupt a 1-byte-element cache with 4-byte writes). Added fused FP8 attention benchmark coverage.
  • Agent tool-call regressions: Fixed three tool-call regression causes from live runs, two Spark agent stalls (whitespace loop, missing turn reopen), KV splice relayout corruption on head-count padding / stride shrink, FP8 scale buffers going stale on spliced stride changes, Spark's end-of-text marker leaking into saved replies, and web_fetch now loading by default at session start.

What's New in 26.4

Apple Foundation Model support:

Chat with Apple's on-device Foundation Model, with live activity indicator, smoothed streaming, and a per-turn history budget so the transcript honors its context window.

/compact Conversation Compaction:

Manual /compact slash command (opencode-style) that folds the conversation into two AFM digests — a rolling general summary plus a detailed recap of recent work — injected into every later prompt on both backends. Transactional (a failed model leaves chat untouched), chunked for long histories, includes tool-call records. Auto-compact on context limits is deliberately deferred to a follow-up.

Settings Glow-up:

Reworked settings into a sidebar-driven layout matching macOS System Settings: sliders + editable numeric fields replacing steppers, shaded group backgrounds, three-per-row sampling controls with precise inputs, and an updated settings guide.
